content: 1. Amikacin's levels or effects may be influenced by the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Nilotinib increases amikacin's levels or effects via this mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Amikacin enhances the effects of onabotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. Aminoglycosides, including amikacin, may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, potentially leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and increased systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 3. Co-administration of amikacin and oxaliplatin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Exercise caution and monitor. 4. Amikacin and paromomycin both elevate the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 5. Amikacin and pentamidine co-administration increases the likelihood of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 6. Amikacin increases peramivir levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution is advised when peramivir is co-administered with nephrotoxic drugs. Monitor closely. 7. Phenobarbital reduces amikacin's levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 8. Phenytoin decreases amikacin's levels or effects through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 9. Co-administration of amikacin and polymyxin B increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Amikacin enhances the effects of prabotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. Aminoglycosides may amplify botulinum toxin effects, potentially causing excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 11. Quercetin reduces amikacin's levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 12. Rifampin decreases amikacin's levels or effects through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 13. Amikacin enhances the effects of rimabotulinumtoxinB via pharmacodynamic synergy. Aminoglycosides may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and increased systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 14. Ritonavir increases amikacin's levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 15. Sirolimus elevates amikacin's levels or effects through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 16. Amikacin reduces the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Antibiotics may decrease efficacy by disrupting colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Use caution and monitor. 17. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride co-administration with amikacin increases toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, raising the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor. 18. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate co-administration with amikacin increases toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, heightening the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor. 19. St. John’s Wort reduces amikacin's levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 20. Co-administration of amikacin and streptomycin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 21. Amikacin and streptozocin co-administration elevates the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 22. Tacrolimus increases amikacin's levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 23. Co-administration of amikacin and tenofovir DF increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Amikacin also raises tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor. 24. Amikacin and tobramycin co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Inhaled tobramycin and amikacin co-administration heightens the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent or sequential use to reduce ototoxicity risk. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Tolvaptan increases amikacin's levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 27. Trazodone reduces amikacin's levels or effects through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 28. Co-administration of amikacin and trimagnesium citrate anhydrous may increase the risk of neuromuscular weakness and paralysis. Use caution and monitor. 29. Amikacin and vancomycin co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 30. Verapamil elevates amikacin's levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 31. Co-administration of amikacin and voclosporin increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Aceclofenac increases amikacin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and primarily occurs in preterm infants. 33. Acemetacin elevates amikacin levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and mainly observed in preterm infants. 34. Co-administration of acyclovir and amikacin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 35. Adefovir and amikacin co-administration heightens the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 36. Amiodarone increases amikacin's levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 37. Co-administration of amikacin and amphotericin B deoxycholate is contraindicated due to increased nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. 38. Aspirin increases amikacin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and primarily occurs in preterm infants.
